algorithm: Enumerate how many largest elements are assigned to a possibly decreased minimum; derive the required decreases by ceiling division.
correctness_argument: For a fixed number c of assignments, replacing the c largest values by the eventual minimum maximizes reduction. Decreasing that common source first reduces c+1 values per decrease. All other changes can be consolidated into this form without more operations.
problem_understanding: Sort values and choose the minimum as the common assignment source.

steps.claim: Sort values and choose the minimum as the common assignment source.
steps.rationale: Sort values and choose the minimum as the common assignment source.

steps.claim: Replacing the smallest targets maximizes sum reduction.
steps.rationale: Replacing the smallest targets maximizes sum reduction.

steps.claim: For a fixed number c of assignments, replacing the c largest values by the eventual minimum maximizes reduction. Decreasing that common source first reduces c+1 values per decrease. All other changes can be consolidated into this form without more operations.
steps.rationale: For a fixed number c of assignments, replacing the c largest values by the eventual minimum maximizes reduction. Decreasing that common source first reduces c+1 values per decrease. All other changes can be consolidated into this form without more operations.

steps.claim: Time: O(n log n); space: O(n).
steps.rationale: Time: O(n log n); space: O(n).

steps.claim: Implementation follows these obligations: Sort values and choose the minimum as the common assignment source. For c assignments, choose the c largest targets. Each decrease of the source saves c+1 in the eventual sum. Ceiling-divide the remaining positive deficit. Minimize c plus decreases over 0 through n-1.
steps.rationale: Implementation follows these obligations: Sort values and choose the minimum as the common assignment source. For c assignments, choose the c largest targets.
